hxloc 2.0.0-alpha.2 — tools for H073.Local

USAGE
  hxloc compile <source> <output> [options]
  hxloc check   <source> [options]
  hxloc import  <xliff> <output> [options]

COMPILE
  Turns a tree of JSON catalogues into compiled LOC3 binaries.
  Run this in your build; ship only the output directory.

    <source>            Directory holding one subdirectory per language.
    <output>            Directory to write .loc3 files into.

    --keys              Keep key names in the binaries. Bigger files, but
                        missing-key reports name the key instead of a hash.
    --language <code>   Compile only this language. Repeatable.
    --clean             Delete the output directory first.
    --quiet             Only print errors.

CHECK
  Compares every language against the reference catalogue and reports
  problems. Exits with code 1 if any are found, so CI fails on them.

    <source>            Directory holding one subdirectory per language.

    --reference <code>  Catalogue to compare against. Defaults to _master,
                        or the language with the most keys if absent.
    --strict            Treat warnings as problems too.
    --quiet             Only print the summary.

IMPORT
  Turns XLIFF 1.2 into a source tree: catalogues plus the schema, since
  XLIFF carries maxwidth and note alongside the text.

    <xliff>             A .xliff/.xlf file, or a directory of them.
    <output>            Directory to write the source tree into.

    --state <name>      Only import units whose target has this state,
                        e.g. translated or final.
    --quiet             Only print errors.

  One file carries a language pair, so an import writes both the source
  and the target catalogue. Plural forms travel as "key[form]" unit ids,
  which is the convention this tool reads and writes -- XLIFF 1.2 has no
  element for them, so without one a round trip turns a key with four
  forms into four unrelated keys.

  Import lands in the source tree rather than compiling directly, s
